To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prolactin receptor short forms (SF), which act as dominant negative inhibitors of the long form of the prolactin receptor (LF), are down-regulated in human breast cancers.
the relative ratio of prolactin short to long receptor forms is decreased in human breast cancer tissues and cell lines.
(1) The prolactin receptor is a key regulator of mammary cell proliferation, and (2) the ratio of inhibitory to stimulatory forms of prolactin is decreased in breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of prolactin and prolactin receptor isoforms in breast tumor development.
the role of prolactin signaling in breast cancer.
a novel mechanism of prolactin action in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ratio of SFs/LF in the breast cancer cells is significantly decreased and that the ratio of expression of prolactins receptor variants is a potential prognostic marker in breast cancer.

prolactin receptor variant expression in breast tumors and cell lines is significantly altered, and the relative decrease in the expression of the short forms compared with the long form could play an important role in breast tumor growth.
the ratio of SFs:LFs is significantly lower in breast cancer tissues/cell lines compared with normal breast tissues/cell lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prolactin receptor expression in human breast tumors is altered in a manner that may contribute to the growth and/or development of the disease.
the prolactin receptor system is a potential therapeutic target in breast cancer.
the ratio of prolactin SFs to LF is significantly decreased in breast cancer tissues and cell lines, which could contribute to the development/progression of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ratio of SFs:LFs is reduced in breast cancer.
prolactin receptor expression is altered in breast cancers.
the expression of the inhibitory SFs of the prolactin receptor is decreased in breast cancer and this may contribute to the development of breast tumors.
